solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Undertaken as a final recourse? Most unlikely, as described by GP

parts.note: the last person you'd expect is the most unlikely one

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the letters GP surround what is described

parts.note: taken as written, a general practitioner

explanation.surface: A doctor's view of a desperate, improbable final treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' means drawn around: G and P enclose AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-gasp effort is one made at the very final moment, a desperate final resort.

clue.text: Fewer working class

parts.note: less means fewer
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Fewer people from the working class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working class' reads as a social group; 'working' is ON and 'class' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a period of teaching, as a class is in a school timetable.

clue.text: Wise guy reformed rascal met

indicators.note: reformed means formed anew, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever man meets a rascal who has changed his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a know-all, a cocky person who thinks themselves clever, a wise guy.

clue.text: Guess one agrees, loosely, about hydrogen and what causes global warming?

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the chemical symbol
loosely means the letters are not held in order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A guess that one roughly agrees about hydrogen as the cause of global warming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' signals the anagram and 'about' wraps its result around the chemical symbol; the question mark marks a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon dioxide, methane and similar gases trap heat in the atmosphere, causing climate change.

clue.text: Person of importance quick to receive me on base

indicators.note: to receive means the word for quick takes the word me inside it

parts.note: soon means quickly, before long
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: An important person is quick to welcome me at the base.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone, as a noun, is a notable person, as in thinking oneself someone.

clue.text: Newspaper chief travelled back to cover it

indicators.note: the reversed word is wrapped around it, covering it on both sides
back tells us the word for travelled is read in reverse

parts.note: rode is a past tense meaning travelled, on horseback or by vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss went back to report on a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives EDOR, and 'to cover' makes it wrap the second piece; 'cover' poses as journalism slang for reporting.
explanation.definitionFit: The editor is the senior journalist in charge of a newspaper's content.

clue.text: What the window tax might have been seen as? A rip-off

definitions.text: What the window tax might have been seen as?
definitions.meaning: Britain once taxed houses by their number of windows, literally charging for daylight
an idiom for a blatant overcharge

explanation.surface: The old window tax was a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: From 1696 to 1851 English householders paid a tax on windows, so it took their daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a shamelessly excessive price, a swindle in broad view.

clue.text: Article on team's leader, a Greek character

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of team is taken

explanation.surface: A news article on a team captain, a Greek personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: See 25
Feel acute embarrassment? Summons ambassador

parts.note: a writ is a legal document such as a summons
HE is His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An ambassador squirms on being served a summons.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist the body in pain, and figuratively to squirm with shame.

clue.text: Box close to stage not required,

parts.note: to spar is to box, especially in practice

indicators.note: the close, or end, of the word stage supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: A theatre box near the stage is going unused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a noun, a theatre seat, but it is the verb spar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spare is surplus, kept over and not needed at present.

clue.text: Cheerful, members finding Jupe's performing dog

parts.note: merry means cheerful
legs are limbs, an old sense of members of the body

explanation.surface: Happy club members find a circus dog belonging to Jupe.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's Hard Times, Signor Jupe is a circus clown whose performing dog is Merrylegs.
explanation.definitionFit: Merrylegs is the trained circus dog of Sissy Jupe's father in Dickens's novel Hard Times.

clue.text: Total published, also revealed

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
and means also, in addition
a secret that is out has been revealed

explanation.surface: A total of what was published and revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out is an adjective meaning complete or utter, as in an out-and-out liar.

clue.text: Mad discarding spades? Senseless

indicators.note: discarding, as at cards, means the letter for spades is thrown out of the word for mad

parts.note: insane means mad
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card player calls it crazy to throw away spades.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture of discarding spades hides the letter deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or lacking sense, so it is a synonym of senseless.

clue.text: Bay — a large bay

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a cove is a small sheltered bay

explanation.surface: A bay is defined, simply, as a large bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Bay' is a recess in a wall, not a stretch of coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay in architecture is a recess in a wall or room, which is what an alcove is.

clue.text: Show former husband one piece

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies
I is the Roman numeral for one
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Someone shows their ex-husband a single piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit something is to display it publicly, a synonym of show as a verb.

clue.text: In abundance after prohibition in Indian city

indicators.note: after means the word for in abundance follows the word for prohibition

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
galore means in abundance, placed after a noun

explanation.surface: Plenty to be had after a ban was lifted in an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore, now Bengaluru, is the capital of the southern Indian state of Karnataka.

clue.text: Stays after winning move

indicators.note: after means the word for stays follows the word for winning

parts.note: a player who is up is ahead, winning
sticks means stays put

explanation.surface: Someone stays on after winning, then moves.
explanation.definitionFit: To up sticks is a British idiom meaning to move house or leave a place suddenly.

clue.text: Constable I included as very good painter

indicators.note: included means the letter I goes inside the abbreviation for the officer

parts.note: PC is the abbreviation for police constable
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: Constable, the painter, is compared with another very good painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' suggests John Constable, the English landscape painter, but here it is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was a celebrated twentieth-century Spanish artist, a great master of modern art.

clue.text: Bloomer old Roman Catholic concealed

parts.note: hid means concealed

explanation.surface: An old Catholic hid a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, but it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant, so in crossword terms it is a bloomer.

clue.text: Second edition — short run

parts.note: a print, or print run, is an edition of a publication

explanation.surface: A second edition had only a short print run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short run' reads as a small printing, but means a fast race over a short distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a race run at full speed over a short distance.

clue.text: Rescue brute, grabbing end of tail

indicators.note: grabbing means the word for brute seizes the letter and holds it inside

parts.note: a savage is a brute

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of tail

explanation.surface: A beast is rescued after grabbing an animal's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is the act of saving goods or a ship from loss, a rescue.

clue.text: Live it up, taking in a show

indicators.note: taking in means the word for live it up holds the letter a inside

parts.note: to revel is to celebrate and live it up

explanation.surface: Partying hard while going to a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like a noun, a performance, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to show or disclose it.

clue.text: Flavour includes whiskey, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: includes means the word for flavour holds the letter for whiskey inside it

parts.note: tang is a sharp flavour
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drink's flavour contains whiskey, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a set phrase meaning so to speak; 'in a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality or regional accent in someone's voice.

clue.text: Main artery forming part of that road going north

indicators.note: going north in a down clue says the hidden letters are read backwards
forming part of means the letters lie inside the words that road

explanation.surface: A main road forms part of that northbound route.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'forming part' in the definition; it is the hiding signal, so the definition is just 'Main artery'. 'going north' reads ATROA upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the largest artery of the body, carrying blood from the heart.

clue.text: Famous person and judge paint the town red

parts.note: celeb is short for celebrity
to rate something is to judge or assess it

explanation.surface: A celebrity and a judge go out for a wild night.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint the town red is an idiom for going out and having a riotous good time.

clue.text: It has restrictions, unfortunately, for a poet

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that verse has unfortunate restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IT HAS RESTRICTIONS rearrange into the poet's full name, entered across two lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina Rossetti was a Victorian English writer of verse, author of Goblin Market.

clue.text: Couple ultimately bound to run away together

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of the word couple is used

parts.note: to lope is to run with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: A couple is eventually bound to run off together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain to', but it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping is running off secretly in order to marry, so the couple leave together.

clue.text: Meagre sum initially held in reserve

indicators.note: held in means the first letter of sum is placed inside the word for reserve

parts.note: spare means reserve, as in a spare tyre

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of sum

explanation.surface: A meagre sum is set aside in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means scanty or thinly spread, a synonym of meagre.

clue.text: In excellent health, I agree

definitions.meaning: a phrase of assent, meaning all right then

explanation.surface: Someone in great health agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes good physical condition and is also a reply accepting a proposal.
